title: The Sexless Innkeeper
cn: 第 4 集 · 无性旅馆老板
novel:
Marshall and Lily wanted to be the [[fun couple|fun couple]] everyone loved. They invited Ted, Barney, and Robin to a [[poetry|poetry]] night at their apartment, complete with cheap wine and [[candles|candle]].

The evening was a [[disaster|disaster]]. Marshall read a poem so [[embarrassing|embarrassing]] that Ted [[pretended|pretend]] to fall asleep. Robin [[yawned|yawn]] openly. Barney escaped through the window.

"We're not fun," Lily [[admitted|admit]] sadly. "We're [[boring|boring]]."

Meanwhile, Barney dated a woman who only wanted to [[cuddle|cuddle]]. She refused every [[advance|advance]] he made. "I just want to hold you," she said.

Barney felt [[trapped|trapped]]. He was, as Ted joked, a "[[sexless|sexless]] [[innkeeper|innkeeper]]," forced to host a guest who would never leave.

In the end, both couples learned a lesson. Marshall and Lily accepted that their kind of fun was quiet and small. And Barney, for once, simply held the woman's hand and said nothing — a [[miracle|miracle]] the gang would talk about for weeks.

fun couple.en: a pair of partners who are lively and amusing

candle.en: a stick of wax with a string that burns to give light

disaster.en: an event that causes great harm or failure

embarrassing.en: making you feel shy or ashamed

pretend.en: to act as if something is true when it is not

yawn.en: to open your mouth wide when you are tired

admit.en: to agree that something is true

cuddle.en: to hold someone close to show love

advance.en: an attempt to start a romantic relationship

trapped.en: unable to escape from a situation

innkeeper.en: a person who owns or runs an inn

miracle.en: a very surprising and lucky event
